text.p: The former president and vice president in charge of sales at Kurzweil Applied Intelligence Inc were sentenced to prison terms for their roles in a scheme to inflate revenues at the company, the U.S. Attorney's office for the District of Massachusetts said on Thursday.

U.S. District Court Judge Richard Stearns sentenced former Kurzweil President Bernard Bradstreet, 51, of Sudbury, Mass., to two years and nine months in prison, followed by two years of supervised release. He was ordered to pay $2.3 million.
Former sales manager Thomas Campbell, 63, of Acton, Mass., was sentenced to one year and six months in prison, to be followed by two years of supervised release.

In May, Bradstreet and Campbell were found guilty of conspiracy, securities fraud and falsifying books and records of the Waltham, Mass., high-technology company, which produces a device capable of recognizing human speech.

Kurzweil released financial statements that exaggerated revenue by including sales that were not yet finalized. That made it appear the company was recording profits when it was actually losing money, the U.S. Attorney's office said.
The false reports included the company's prospectus for its initial public offering and quarterly financial reports for two quarters in 1993.
Kurzweil's former treasurer, Debra Murray, previously entered a guilty plea to charges related to the scheme. She was sentenced in June to three years of probation and to community service.
